newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Buy U.S. if Fed raises rates.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Buy U.S. if Fed raises rates.

text.p: Any U.S. interest rate rise next week may provide investors with an ideal opportunity to jump into Treasuries out of European debt markets, economists said on Wednesday.
European economies are expected to take over the mantle of growth from the U.S. sometime in the second half of the year, a move seen pushing the T-bond/Bund spread closer over the longer term.

"If the U.S. did hike rates next week, while you might see some negative reaction in the Treasury market, in the much bigger picture the spread could widen back out to 115, 120 basis points," said Graham McDevitt head of bond strategy at Paribas Capital Markets.
"But we would see this a tremendous buying opportunity."
U.S treasury prices have wilted recently at the prospect of a possibile interest rate rise at next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.
But some analysts said they did not expect a rise as early as that -- a sentiment reinforced by Wednesday's unexpectedly sharp drop in April producer prices.

"Last night a couple of comments from some Fed officials again worried the market and we still think the U.S. is going to be hiking rates, but the odds have moved away from May and towards July and the market has also done that," said McDevitt.
By 1315 GMT, June T-bond futures were up 12/32 at 110-06 and the 10-year T-note/Bund gap was at 109 basis points, compared with 107 at Tuesday's close.

Analysts said in the long-term, the timing of the rate rise was not as important as the strength of U.S. economic data over the next few weeks which would give an indication as to the pace of the U.S economy's growth.

Stephen Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking, said April's economic data was showing a slowdown from the rapid rate of growth in March and was likely to create a bit of uncertainty in the minds of FOMC members as to the need for an immediate rate hike.

Many economists said they expected U.S. economic growth to slow in the second half while seeing a pick-up in European economies. The end of the year could be strong for European bonds but a good time to buy into U.S. bond markets, they said.
"A series of rate hikes and the level of bond yields in the U.S. should slow the U.S. economy in the second half and that should be good news for the bond market," McDevitt said.

"If we get a rate hike next week and the spread ballooned back out towards the highs at 120 we'd be recommending people switch out of Europe into the U.S. on a longer ternm basis looking for a significant spread convergence."
Strategists said the question being asked was when, not if, a rate hike would happen.
With the market currently pricing in a change in July from the Fed funds' present 5.50 percent, a move next week could certainly have a near-term negative impact on the U.S bond market.

"In some ways it doesn't change that much whether they go next week or they don't because we are still looking for a further Fed tightening over the summer," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe. "But we'd still get a sell-off on a rate hike."
McDevitt said in the incidence of a rate rise on May 20 it would be the short end of the Treasury curve that would suffer most.

"The curve would flatten because the short end would get hit. The short end has taken out most of the pricing in of a rate hike so the short end would definitely get hit. The bonds might also be negative but less so," he said.
